title: Introduce lightweight Go RAG playground and typed toolchain samples
author: Marta Kozlowski
release_notes: Add a compact Go RAG playground that demonstrates Go SDK usage, typed tool contracts, local telemetry probes, and an offline dev runner for iterative debugging.
description:
Summary: This PR adds a small, opinionated Go quickstart that demonstrates building a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) micro-playground using the Go SDK, typed tool contracts, and a local dev runner with built-in telemetry probes. Motivation: we have many TS/Python examples; several customers and internal SDK advocates asked for a concise Go-first example that focuses on: 1) typed tool calling with contract validation, 2) a minimal local runner for fast feedback loops (no cloud infra required), and 3) lightweight telemetry hooks that show what to surface in Redwood Console. What changed (high level): - new example: examples/go/rag-playground/ containing README, main.go, tool_contracts.go, dev-runner (small binary stub), and sample dataset - docs: docs/examples/go-rag-quickstart.md added to the docs site tree - tests: integration smoke test that runs the dev-runner against a seeded in-memory index - CI: workflow updated to run Go example smoke tests on linux-amd64 Scope & trade-offs: This example intentionally keeps things small: it uses a tiny in-memory vector store and a mock tool (webhook echo) rather than production connectors. The goal is developer onboarding rather than production readiness. Checklist: - [x] Add example code + README with step-by-step local run instructions - [x] Add typed tool contract definitions and contract linter config - [x] Add smoke test and CI job - [x] Add docs site page and quickstart guide - [x] Add telemetry probe examples and wiring Usage: See examples/go/rag-playground/README.md for step-by-step instructions. Typical flow: 1) go run ./examples/go/rag-playground/main.go --local-index 2) open the dev-runner web UI at http://localhost:8080 to send prompts and inspect prefix cache / telemetry 3) use ./scripts/seed-index to load sample docs Commits (summary): - init: add go module and example scaffold - feature: main runner and typed tool contracts - test: add smoke tests and fixtures - docs: add quickstart page and images - ci: add workflow for go-examples Smoke test notes: The smoke test instantiates the dev-runner with a deterministic seed and asserts that: - a simple query returns 3 retrieval hits - the tool call mock responds with a 200 echo - telemetry events (request.start, retrieval.complete, generation.complete) are emitted to a local file sink (used by the smoke test) Local development steps (condensed): 1) Install Go 1.21+ 2) cd examples/go/rag-playground && go run ./main.go --dev 3) In another terminal run: curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/query -d '{"q":"what is redwood inference"}' Example snippet (from main.go): "// small example: create client and run a retrieval-augmented prompt
client := redwood.NewClient(os.Getenv(\"REDWOOD_API_KEY\"))
resp, _ := client.Generate(ctx, &redwood.GenerateRequest{Model: \"rw-compact-1\", Prompt: prompt})
fmt.Println(resp.Text)" Related: ENG-1042 (Go SDK ergonomics) and internal examples backlog. Migration/rollout: This is additive. No infra changes required. Follow-ups: - Add an example showing dedicated/private deployment wiring - Expand the dev-runner to optionally persist telemetry to a mock console - Add interactive web UI for tool-call inspection
